Each Verbal Ability question carries 2 marks, each General Studies question carries 3 marks and each Data Interpretation question carries 5 marks.The total marks from the Verbal Ability section make up at least 60% of the overall marks. If Data Interpretation section contains 16 questions and General Studies section carries at least 20% of the overall marks, which of the following best describes the number of questions in General Studies Section?

A juice seller has two types of juice. One is freshly extracted juice, which contains 75% water, and the other is concentrated juice, which contains only 20% water. The seller takes 25 liters of concentrated juice and adds water to it until the mixture has the same proportion of water content as the fresh juice. He sells this reconstituted juice at the same price as the cost price of the concentrated juice. What is the total profit percentage gained through this method?

In a game show, there are two boxes: one red and one blue. The Red Box contains 5 red balls and 7 blue balls, while the Blue Box contains 4 red balls and 6 blue balls. A box is randomly chosen, and a ball is drawn from that box. The ball drawn is red. What is the probability that the ball came from the Red Box, given that it is red?

Two friends, Riya and Rahul, planned a journey from Pune to Jaipur. Rahul started on a motorbike at a speed of 40 km/h, while Riya began her journey in a car, travelling faster at 60 km/h. However, after driving for 3.5 hours, Riya’s car broke down. She spent half an hour trying to fix it but couldn’t get it running. Fortunately, a truck came by, and she got a lift for another 500 km in the truck. The truck moved at a speed of 45 km/h. After this ride, Riya still had 200 km left to reach Jaipur by road. Instead of continuing by road, she took a shortcut of just 100 km and ran the rest of the way at a speed of 30 km/h.

Suppose Riya’s car had broken down at the point where she was dropped off by the truck, and she had immediately taken the shortcut, then by approximately how many kilometers would she have beaten Rahul to Jaipur?

Five different teams—X, Y, Z, P, and Q—booked a conference room on different days from Monday to Friday. Each team conducted a different type of session: Training, Workshop (WS), Client Meeting (CM), Brainstorming, and Review (RS). Additional information is given below:

  • Two teams booked the conference room between Team Z and Team Y.
  • There were three days between the teams that booked the room for Training and Brainstorming.
  • Team X did a client meeting and booked the room just after Team P.
  • P did not conduct a Review session.
  • Team Z and Team Q did not conduct a Brainstorming session.
  • The number of teams that booked the room before Y is more than those that booked after Y.
  • P did not book the conference room on Monday.

Which team booked the conference room on Monday?

A car of mass m=1000 kg is moving along a curved road of radius r=50 m at a constant speed of v=20 m/s. The road is banked at an angle of 60∘ to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the tires and the road is μ=0.3. Assume the car does not slip while taking the turn.

Calculate the centripetal force required to keep the car moving in a circle.
Determine the normal force and the frictional force acting on the car.

The centripetal force, FC is given as follows:

<inlineMath>{F_C} = \frac{{m{v^2}}}{r}</inlineMath> where 

m is the mass of the car, v is the speed of the car, and r is the radius of the curve

Friction is assumed to oppose the relative motion (or potential slip). If the car tends to slide up, friction acts down the incline. The frictional force, f is given as follows:

f=−μN

μ is the coefficient of friction, and N is the normal force.

Vertical direction (no vertical acceleration):

Ncosθ=mg+fsinθ

Horizontal direction (provides centripetal acceleration):

<inlineMath>Nsin\theta  + fcos\theta  = \frac{{m{v^2}}}{r}</inlineMath>

A man is standing on the edge of a cliff that is 80 meters high. At the same instant:

  • He throws a ball upward with a velocity of 20 m/s.
  • Another person at the bottom of the cliff throws a second ball upward with a velocity of 40 m/s.

Assume acceleration due to gravity g=10 m/s2. (take upward direction as positive).

After how much time will the two balls cross paths?
At what height from the ground will they meet?

Formulas (for vertical motion under gravity)

For any object under uniform acceleration (gravity):

<inlineMath>s(t) = {s_o} + ut + \frac{1}{2}a{t^2}</inlineMath> 

Where:

  • s(t) = position at time t
  • so​ = initial position
  • u = initial velocity
  • a = acceleration (use −g if upward is positive)
  • t = time

Two rowing teams, Team A and Team B, train on a river. Team A rows downstream from a fixed point for 30 minutes and then rows back upstream for 40 minutes to return to the same point. Team B, using a slightly faster boat, completes the same downstream and upstream distances in 25 and 35 minutes, respectively. The speed of the river is 3 km/h.
Who rows faster in still water, and by how much? What is the distance Team A covers downstream?

A swimming pool can be filled by two inlets, Pipe P and Pipe Q, in 60 minutes and 20 minutes, respectively. If both inlets are opened together, the pool should be filled in less time. Whistle-blowing, the act of exposing unethical or illegal activities within an organisation, remains a deeply complex ethical issue. On one hand, whistle-blowers play a crucial role in holding institutions accountable, preventing harm to the public, and ensuring transparency. Their actions can lead to important reforms in areas like healthcare, finance, and government. On the other hand, critics argue that whistle-blowing can violate loyalty to one’s employer, breach confidentiality, and disrupt workplace cohesion. 

In recent years, legal protections for whistle-blowers have strengthened in many countries, acknowledging their value in democratic societies. Laws such as the U.S. Whistleblower Protection Act aim to safeguard individuals who speak out in good faith. However, the effectiveness of these laws often depends on organisational culture and public support. 

Which of the following statements most strongly reflects an opposing viewpoint to whistle-blowing, as inferred from the passage?

options.text: Whistle-blowers initiate reforms but may unintentionally damage the very systems they seek to improve.
Legal protections empower whistle-blowers to act in defence of public interest.
Internal ethical culture can reduce the need for whistle-blowing altogether.
Whistle-blowing upholds moral responsibility above institutional loyalty.

questions.questionText:
Tariffs, traditionally viewed as a means of economic protectionism, have increasingly become a double-edged sword in modern global trade. While they aim to support domestic industries by making foreign goods more expensive, the broader economic effects often raise critical concerns. Tariffs can lead to costlier raw materials and finished products, indirectly burdening domestic producers and consumers alike. 
In highly interconnected global markets, such measures may distort supply chains, provoke retaliatory tariffs, and reduce overall trade efficiency. Policymakers must therefore weigh immediate political or economic gains against the long-term risks of reduced competitiveness and strained international ties. Tariffs may serve strategic purposes, but are rarely without economic trade-offs.
What higher-order conclusion can be drawn from the passage about the use of tariffs in a globally interconnected economy?

options.text: Tariffs, though politically expedient, can introduce hidden inefficiencies that outweigh their intended benefits in open-market economies.
The imposition of tariffs is primarily a symbolic gesture, lacking measurable impact in interconnected trade networks.
Long-term national prosperity is best secured through sustained tariff regimes that prioritise domestic production over global collaboration.
Tariff policies serve as neutral tools that affect all economies symmetrically, regardless of their size or integration level.

questions.questionText:
Evaporation is the process by which liquid water turns into vapour and enters the atmosphere. Several factors influence the rate of evaporation. One key factor is temperature; higher temperatures provide more energy for water molecules to escape into the air. Wind speed also affects evaporation; moving air removes the saturated layer of water vapour near the surface, allowing more evaporation to occur. Humidity plays a role as well when the air is already full of moisture, as evaporation slows down. Additionally, surface area matters; water spread over a larger area evaporates more quickly than in a limited space. These factors together determine how quickly water evaporates from surfaces in nature and daily life.

Which of the following statements best supports the information presented in the passage?

options.text: Evaporation occurs faster in humid conditions because moisture levels are already high.
A smaller surface area increases the rate of evaporation by concentrating heat.
Wind helps increase evaporation by removing moisture-saturated air near the surface.
Lower temperatures provide more energy for water molecules to evaporate quickly.

questions.questionText:
Space exploration represents one of humanity’s most ambitious pursuits, driven by curiosity, technological advancement, and the quest to understand our place in the Universe. Since the launch of Sputnik in 1957 and the first Moon landing in 1969, space missions have expanded to include robotic explorations of Mars, deep-space telescopes like the James Webb, and plans for human settlements on the Moon and beyond. These efforts have led to scientific discoveries that benefit not only astronomy but also life on Earth, including innovations in communication, materials science, and medicine.

However, space exploration also presents formidable challenges. It requires massive financial investment, advanced technology, and careful risk management, especially when human life is involved. Ethical concerns about space mining, planetary contamination, and the militarisation of space continue to spark global debate. While space remains a frontier of infinite possibilities, its exploration demands responsible planning, international cooperation, and a balance between ambition and sustainability.

Which of the following best summarises the passage ?

options.text: Space exploration, while often celebrated for its technological advancements, primarily functions as a geopolitical tool driven by national competition and resource ambition.
The continued pursuit of space missions reflects a paradox: humanity's desire to expand its horizons is both a source of innovation and a driver of complex ethical and financial dilemmas.
Although space exploration has historically offered benefits to Earth, its modern trajectory reveals diminishing returns, raising questions about its long-term value.
The risks and controversies associated with space missions outweigh their contributions, suggesting that further investment in space is unjustifiable.

questions.questionText:
The telegraph and fax machine played major roles in revolutionising long-distance communication. The telegraph, developed in 19th century, was the first technology to allow instant messaging across great distances. Using Morse code, it enabled people to send information quickly through wires, changing how news, business, and government operations functioned. It reduced the delay of days or weeks in communication to just minutes. 

The fax machine, which became popular in the 20th century, allowed the transmission of scanned printed materials over telephone lines. This was especially useful in offices, as documents could be shared without physical delivery. Fax machines combined speed with the ability to send visual content like signatures, diagrams and hand-written notes.   

Which of the following best explains a cause-and-effect relationship from the passage?

options.text: The invention of the fax machine caused the disappearance of handwritten letters.
The need for faster communication led to the invention and use of the telegraph and fax, which greatly reduced delays in message delivery.
The popularity of email directly caused the creation of the telegraph.
The use of Morse code caused visual content to become more common in communication.

questions.questionText:
In everyday situations, reason plays a key role in helping individuals make fair and thoughtful decisions. Whether it's a manager deciding how to resolve a workplace conflict or a teacher handling a case of student misconduct, logical thinking helps assess facts, understand consequences, and choose the most responsible course of action. Using reason helps avoid impulsive choices and ensures that decisions are consistent and justifiable. However, real-world decisions are rarely made with logic alone. Emotions, values, and personal relationships often influence how people respond to ethical challenges. 

For example, a supervisor may struggle to discipline a close colleague even when it's the logical thing to do. While emotions add depth to decision-making, relying on reason helps maintain fairness and objectivity. In this way, reason serves as a stabilising guide in complex ethical situations.

What is the tone of the passage?

Launched in 2015 by the Government of India, the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (BBBP) campaign aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote the education and empowerment of girls. Rooted in growing concerns over gender discrimination and female foeticide, the initiative seeks to create awareness at the grassroots level and improve girls’ access to education. Through joint efforts by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and the Ministry of Education, the program integrates advocacy, enforcement of legal measures, and local community involvement.

While the campaign has received praise for spotlighting gender inequality, critics argue that implementation gaps and insufficient funding limit its long-term impact. Nonetheless, BBBP remains a symbolic and strategic effort toward a more inclusive and gender-equal society.

Which of the following best supports the objectives of the 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' initiative?

options.text: Encouraging early marriage to protect girls from urban risks.
Promoting gender-sensitive education and community awareness programs.
Limiting girls’ access to co-educational institutions.
Offering incentives only to families with male children.

International standard philosophy refers to global norms, principles, and frameworks that guide countries' ethics, governance, training, and enterprise practices. These standards ensure consistency, equity, and efficiency in various fields, promoting cooperation and mutual knowledge-sharing amongst one-of-a-kind cultures and societies.

International standards like ISO (International Organisation for Standardisation) help ensure great product quality, safety, and environmental sustainability in industries. In training programs, philosophical frameworks combined with human rights principles and some ethical reasoning are integrated into the curriculum to encourage critical thinking and promote global citizenship. Similarly, in governance, standards like democracy, justice, and equality shape the foundation of worldwide legal guidelines and diplomatic corps. 

Which statement best summarises the passage?

options.text: International standards only apply to industries, ensuring product quality and safety.
Local traditions are more important than international standards, making them ineffective.
International standards have little influence on modern society.
International standard philosophy promotes global consistency in ethics, governance, education, and industry.

questions.questionText:
English literature has journeyed over centuries, reflecting the changing instances, values, and voices of society. It started with Old English, a language barely recognisable to modern readers, in works like Beowulf, in which testimonies of heroism and myth ruled. This period changed into observed usage of Middle English, wherein writers like Geoffrey Chaucer, together with his Canterbury Tales, started to shape extra relatable characters and social observation. 

The Renaissance generation introduced a burst of creativity led by literary giants like William Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe. Themes of love, strength, betrayal, and human nature took the middle stage, and drama flourished. The richness of language and exploration of the human situation made this era unforgettable.

From historic epics to postmodern narratives, English literature has evolved into a rich mosaic, with each era including new colours, voices, and meanings to the tapestry of human expression.

 

Which of the following best summarises the passage on the evolution of English literature?

options.text: English literature started with Old English poetry and eventually gave rise to modern science fiction and fantasy genres.
English literature has remained largely traditional in style and content, with few significant changes in theme or structure.
From ancient myths to modern diversity, English literature has evolved by adapting to changing historical, social, and cultural contexts across centuries.
English literature was dominated by British authors until the 20th century, when American literature began to take over completely.

questions.questionText:
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), launched in 2001, is a flagship program by the Government of India aimed at the universalisation of elementary education. The initiative was created to fulfil the mandate of the 86th Constitutional Amendment, which made free and compulsory education an essential right for children aged from 6 to 14 years. SSA seeks to bridge social, regional, and gender gaps by means of ensuring inclusive education for all, especially that specialise in marginalised and disadvantaged communities. The program includes the development of colleges, recruitment of qualified teachers, the availability of learning materials and school infrastructure. 

It promotes network participation via School Management Committees and supports programs for youngsters with special needs. Despite remarkable enhancements in enrolment and access to faculties, SSA has faced criticism for inconsistent implementation across states, loss of trained teachers, and challenges in improving learning outcomes. Nevertheless, it remains a great step toward instructional fairness and literacy in India.

Which of the following best represents a supporting argument for the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan?

options.text: The program has led to increased school enrolment and improved access to education across India.
Learning outcomes remain poor despite increased enrolment under the program.
There is a lack of uniform implementation and teacher training across various states.
The scheme has been criticised for not adequately addressing the needs of differently-abled students.

questions.questionText:
London, with its blend of historical grandeur and contemporary flair, has long been a magnet for travellers from across the globe. From the regal majesty of Buckingham Palace to the modern spectacle of the London Eye, the city seamlessly bridges past and present. Its diverse neighbourhoods, each with unique cultural flavours, offer something for every type of visitor. Yet, London’s appeal goes beyond its attractions; it lies in the experience it provides. 
Whether navigating its world-class transport, strolling through Hyde Park, or discovering street art in Shoreditch, tourists often find themselves immersed in both local charm and global influence. This rich layering of heritage, innovation, and inclusivity makes London not just a place to visit, but one to remember. 
Based on the passage, what can be inferred about the kind of experience London offers to tourists?

options.text: A transformative journey that connects individuals with both cultural depth and cosmopolitan energy.
A predictable tour of iconic sites without significant engagement with modern urban life.
A limited experience focused more on aesthetics than on interactive cultural immersion.
A rushed exploration driven by a checklist of historical monuments and royal attractions.

questions.questionText:
John Locke, a 17th-century English philosopher, is regarded as one of the most influential thinkers in the development of modern political and epistemological theories. Often called the "Father of Liberalism," Locke emphasised individual rights, government by consent, and the separation of powers. His ideas, particularly those in Two Treatises of Government, laid the foundation for democratic principles, advocating that governments should protect life, liberty, and property. In his work An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, he explored the nature of human knowledge, proposing that the mind is a blank slate (tabula rasa) shaped by experience. Locke’s philosophies significantly influenced the American and French Revolutions, shaping constitutional democracies worldwide.

According to the passage, which statement best summarises the passage?

options.text: John Locke was a political leader who advocated for the overthrow of monarchies.
Locke’s ideas on governance and human knowledge contributed to democratic principles.
Locke opposed democracy and believed in absolute monarchy.
John Locke’s primary focus was on religious reforms rather than political philosophy.

questions.questionText:
Passage:

The unification of Germany in the 19th century was a major turning point in European history. Before unification, the region consisted of numerous independent German-speaking states, loosely connected through the German Confederation. The process of unification was largely driven by Otto von Bismarck, the Prime Minister of Prussia, who used a combination of diplomacy and military strategy to achieve this goal.

Bismarck orchestrated three key wars: the Danish War (1864), the Austro-Prussian War (1866), and the Franco-Prussian War (1870–71) to rally German states around Prussia and isolate Austria and France. The victory over France in the Franco-Prussian War stirred strong nationalist feelings among the German people and paved the way for the declaration of the German Empire in 1871 at the Palace of Versailles.

Which of the following best represents a cause-and-effect relationship related to the unification of Germany?

options.text: The German Empire was declared, so Otto von Bismarck became Prime Minister.
The Franco-Prussian War enhanced German nationalist tendencies, leading to unification.
Germany was unified, so Bismarck launched the Austro-Prussian War.
France declared war on Prussia because the German Empire was already unified.

questions.questionText:
Chemical reactions are processes in which substances, known as reactants, undergo changes to form new substances called products. These reactions involve the breaking and forming of chemical bonds between atoms and molecules. Although there are different types of reactions, each type of reaction follows specific patterns and can be influenced by factors such as temperature, pressure, concentration, and the presence of catalysts. For instance, in a combustion reaction, a substance reacts with oxygen to release energy in the form of heat and light, as seen when fossil fuels burn. 

Chemical reactions are central to many processes in both nature and industry, from respiration in living organisms to the manufacturing of various chemicals. Understanding these reactions helps in optimising processes and developing new technologies.

In light of the above, which of the following statements best summarises the passage?

options.text: Chemical reactions are unpredictable processes that do not follow any specific patterns and occur only under extreme conditions.
All chemical reactions are similar, and they occur spontaneously without any external influences or specific patterns.
Chemical reactions involve the transformation into products and can be classified into various types, each influenced by specific factors.
Chemical reactions primarily occur in industrial settings and have occasional relevance to biological processes or natural systems.

questions.questionText:
The Partition of Bengal in 1905, planned by the British under Lord Curzon, was a pivotal moment in the history of Indian nationalism. This event, officially justified as an administrative measure, was widely perceived as a deliberate attempt to divide Bengal along religious lines, weakening the unity of the growing nationalist movement. The move sparked widespread protests across India, with leaders and citizens alike condemning it as an act of colonial manipulation. The Swadeshi Movement emerged in response, urging Indians to boycott British goods and promote indigenous industries. This period marked a significant shift in the tone of Indian nationalism, moving from moderate petitions to more assertive resistance. Despite the eventual reversal of the partition in 1911, the event left an indelible mark on the nationalist psyche, fuelling a stronger and more united demand for self-rule.

After reading the passage, select the correct tone of the passage.

The evolution of science and technology has been a transformative force in shaping modern civilisation. Over the centuries, humanity has witnessed several advances, from the discovery of fire and the wheel to the advent of the internet and artificial intelligence. Early innovations, such as the printing press in the 15th century, revolutionised communication, making knowledge accessible to a wider audience and spurring the Renaissance. In the 20th century, the development of electricity, nuclear energy, and the invention of the computer marked the dawn of the Information Age. These innovations laid the foundation for an interconnected world, where the rapid pace of technological change is now driven by advancements in quantum computing, biotechnology, and nanotechnology. Despite the benefits, the rapid evolution of science and technology has raised concerns about ethical dilemmas, such as privacy issues, environmental impact, and the potential for increased inequality. As we move forward, society must balance innovation with responsibility to ensure technology serves the common good without compromising fundamental human values.

Which of the following best summarises the main idea of the passage?

options.text: The passage describes the decline of human values in the face of scientific progress and highlights the dangers of rapid technological growth.
The passage focuses on the rapid pace of technological advancements and emphasises the need for ethical considerations and responsibility in the future.
The main idea of the passage is the development of new technologies like quantum computing and nanotechnology, which have revolutionised human society.
The evolution of science and technology has been a gradual process that has improved communication and transportation throughout history.

questions.questionText:
Memory is not a perfect recording of the past but a flexible reconstruction. Studies show that each time we recall an event, we reshape it, making memories vulnerable to suggestion and distortion. In courtrooms, eyewitness testimonies, often treated as factual, can be influenced by stress, leading questions, or repeated interrogation.

Psychologist Elizabeth Loftus showed how even subtle wording could implant false memories. With advances in neuroscience, the possibility of editing memories raises serious ethical concerns. If memory can be altered, how reliable is truth in testimonies, and can justice built on memory be trusted?

What is the most appropriate tone of the passage?

Throughout history, various countries have experienced governance under monarchies or military rule. Monarchies, often hereditary, centre power in a royal family with traditions that can foster national unity or suppress reform. In contrast, military regimes emerge when armed forces seize power, usually in response to political instability or perceived corruption. While both systems may bring short-term stability, critics argue they often lack democratic accountability, limit civil freedoms, and centralise decision-making. 
Proponents, however, contend that these regimes can ensure discipline, order, and continuity during turbulent times. The impact of either system depends largely on the context in which they arise and the extent to which they evolve or resist modernisation.
Which of the following statements best presents a well-reasoned argument opposing monarchy and military rule based on the passage?

options.text: Monarchies preserve national heritage and stability across generations.
Military regimes can effectively address corruption and bring swift governance.
Both monarchy and military rule may undermine democratic participation and civil liberties.
Hereditary monarchs and military leaders provide continuity during crises.

questions.questionText:
The British East India Company (EIC) was established in 1600 as a trading company; however, it performed an essential function in the British colonisation of India. Initially, the organisation traded in spices, textiles, and different items; however, over the years, it acquired political and naval power to manipulate big territories in India.

The business enterprise’s rule had both positive and negative impacts. On the one hand, it brought modern-day infrastructure, railways, a postal system, and structured legal machinery, contributing to India’s long-term development. It also facilitated global trade, making India a key part of the British imperial economic system.

On the other hand, the EIC was ordinarily driven by profit, frequently exploiting India's resources for the benefit of the British. Heavy taxation, financial rules favouring British industries, and oppressive land sales systems caused pervasive poverty and economic distress. The organisation additionally suppressed local industries and aggravated numerous famines due to its exploitative regulations.

Which of the following is an argument in support of the British East India Company’s rule in India?

options.text: It introduced modern infrastructure like railways and a legal system
It imposed high taxes and drained India’s resources.
It suppressed local industries and caused economic distress.
Its exploitative policies contributed to widespread poverty.
